einzeiler: Film Threat reviews Akira, Onslaught, The Runner, and more, plus an interview with I…
kurzfassung: Chris Gore and Alan Ng celebrate hitting 169k YouTube subscribers and discuss recent film industry news, including Joseph Kahn's op-ed on Paramount and Warner Bros. potentially leaving Los Angeles. They review several new releases, such as Bruce Campbell's Ernie & Emma, By Any Means, Onslaught, the 4K IMAX rerelease of Akira, Gal Gadot's The Runner, and Fall 2: Deadpoint. The episode also features an interview with Tyler Mann and Rachel DeRouen, the filmmakers behind the indie comedy-thriller I Voted.
stichpunkte: Celebration of reaching 169,000 YouTube subscribers on the channel
Discussion of Joseph Kahn's op-ed regarding Paramount and Warner Bros. potentially relocating out of Los Angeles
AMC Theatres launches Leawood Films, a new indie film distribution label
Review of Bruce Campbell's heartfelt indie drama Ernie & Emma
Review of the civil rights era thriller By Any Means, starring Giancarlo Esposito and Y’lan Noel
Review of the stylized action film Onslaught
Discussion of the 4K IMAX rerelease of the 1988 anime classic Akira and the upcoming documentary Akira: The Documentary
Interview with Tyler Mann and Rachel DeRouen, the married filmmaking team behind I Voted
Review of the real-time thriller The Runner starring Gal Gadot
Review of the survival sequel Fall 2: Deadpoint

clips.hook: The IP is worth more than the sound stages
clips.text: The physical infrastructure of a studio holds far less financial value than major intellectual properties like Harry Potter, Star Trek, or DC, which can be managed from anywhere.

clips.hook: A micro-budget indie beating Star Wars
clips.text: An extremely low-budget independent film managed to outperform a major Star Wars release at the box office, generating massive profits.

clips.hook: Don't hang out with the Grim Reaper
clips.text: Following the discussion of close relatives passing away, the hosts joke that Chris has an eerie habit of being present during tragic losses.

clips.hook: An iconic voting symbol gets a bloody twist
clips.text: The idea for the movie's key marketing image came from seeing a familiar civic sticker right after leaving a stressful polling place lockdown.

clips.hook: Practical mountain sets instead of green screens
clips.text: The production team built a physical rock climbing set rather than relying on computer graphics or blue screens, which explains why the danger feels so authentic.
